doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: Looking through Marty's photographs and goodbyes
summary: Marty shows family photos and pictures of Astor, Manne and Chico Marx, and the interview ends.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Can we tell that guy to hold on?
Yeah, well thanks for your time. It’s been fantastic.
Did you want to look at anything at all?

Let me see what we’ve got here, I don’t know. Stop me when you see something you like. This is my father playing piano, my uncle Phil playing trumpet, my uncle Georgie playing violin, my first house, my first group, my first big band. My father used to do things like that. This is my father, my uncle, my mother.

That’s what everybody says, is that you? That’s why I had to quit. When I was going to Europe with Peanuts Hucko, we had the program notes, and after the concert people would come in the office into the dressing room and they would open up the program to your picture — oh there’s Trummy Young — and when they came to me they were looking to the picture. Oh now here we are, is that you? I said that’s it, I’ve got to get some new pictures. That’s my wife when I met her. This is Bob Astor, Shelly Manne, Chico Marx. There’s Chico with my wife and I when we were kids. This is Mel Torme.
Well let me get some shots of these why don’t we wrap up. And we’ll see if we can go with that. That’s terrific. Thanks.
Thank you, Monk, you’re beautiful. Thank you very much, it’s very comforting. You made me talk more than I should have.

Well because you know how it is, like I remember watching the Johnny Carson show when somebody on the show would say “yeah well you’re making a new movie, right?” And the guy would say, “yeah.” Ooh God, okay, next case. So you need it.
